title: Iraq invades Kuwait
description: Iraqi forces invade Kuwait, putting Kuwaiti and regional Gulf supply at risk

title: Lehman Brothers collapses
description: Financial crisis escalates into a global demand-destruction shock

title: US-led invasion of Iraq begins
description: Invasion of a major producer; heavily telegraphed for months beforehand

title: Libyan civil war begins and production halts
description: Uprising escalates into civil war, removing Libyan output from the market

title: OPEC declines to cut production
description: OPEC opts not to reduce output despite falling prices, signalling a defence of market share

title: OPEC agrees to cut production
description: First coordinated cut since 2008, ending the market-share strategy

title: US withdraws from JCPOA and reimposes Iran sanctions
description: US exits the nuclear deal, signalling restoration of oil sanctions on Iran

title: US sanctions on PDVSA
description: Sanctions target Venezuelan state oil company exports

title: Attack on Saudi Abqaiq and Khurais facilities
description: Aerial attack temporarily removes a large share of Saudi processing capacity

title: US strike kills Qassem Soleimani
description: Sharp US-Iran escalation raising fears of regional conflict and Hormuz risk

title: OPEC+ talks collapse and price war begins
description: Russia and Saudi Arabia fail to agree cuts, triggering a market-share price war into collapsing demand

title: WHO declares COVID-19 a pandemic
description: Global demand destruction as economies shut down; confounded with the OPEC+ price war

title: OPEC+ agrees record production cut
description: Historic ~9.7 million b/d cut agreed in response to pandemic oversupply. NOTE: EIA dates the agreement 15 April - verify exact date

title: Ever Given blocks the Suez Canal
description: Container ship grounds and blocks a chokepoint carrying roughly 10% of seaborne oil trade

title: Russia launches full-scale invasion of Ukraine
description: Invasion raises prospect of sanctions on and disruption to a top-three global producer; heavily anticipated

title: Nord Stream pipelines sabotaged
description: Multiple ruptures detected in Nord Stream 1 and 2, severing a major Russia-Europe gas route

title: EU seaborne embargo and G7 price cap take effect
description: EU ban on seaborne Russian crude plus a $60 G7 price cap enter into force

title: OPEC+ announces surprise voluntary cuts
description: Unscheduled announcement of additional voluntary production cuts

title: Hamas attack on Israel and onset of Gaza war
description: Major Middle East escalation raising regional conflict and supply-risk premia

title: Houthi attacks disrupt Red Sea shipping
description: Attacks on commercial shipping divert traffic from Bab el-Mandeb; crude flows through the chokepoint fell ~18% in Dec 2023 and over 50% in early 2024

title: Operation Desert Storm air campaign begins
description: US-led coalition begins the air war on Iraq after the Jan 15 UN withdrawal deadline; puts Iraqi and Kuwaiti crude and the wider Gulf risk premium in play. DRAFT coding, awaiting Joe's review.

title: Operation Desert Fox airstrikes on Iraq
description: Four days of US/UK airstrikes on Iraqi military and WMD targets during the UNSCOM inspections crisis; Iraqi exports were sanction-limited then, so expected supply disruption was moderate. DRAFT coding.

title: September 11 terrorist attacks
description: Coordinated attacks on the US; the oil channel is mainly a demand and risk shock (aviation collapse, recession fear) rather than a producer supply loss. Joe may reclassify type as demand_shock. DRAFT coding.

title: Israel-Hezbollah (Second Lebanon) war begins
description: Hezbollah cross-border raid triggers a 34-day war; neither party is an oil producer, so the channel is a regional risk premium and fear of wider Iran involvement. Sourced to the UN resolution that ended the war. DRAFT coding.

title: Russia-Georgia war
description: Russia (a top-three crude producer) invades Georgia, the transit state for the BTC pipeline carrying Caspian crude to market; pipeline and transit risk is the oil channel. DRAFT coding.

title: Saudi-led intervention in Yemen (Operation Decisive Storm)
description: Saudi Arabia, the world's largest crude exporter, leads a coalition air campaign in Yemen; the channel is Saudi involvement plus Bab-el-Mandeb transit risk near the Red Sea. DRAFT coding.

title: Gulf of Oman tanker attacks
description: Two oil/product tankers struck near the Strait of Hormuz amid US-Iran tensions; attribution to Iran was asserted but contested (hence medium confidence). Channel is chokepoint and shipping risk. DRAFT coding.

title: Iran's first direct missile and drone strike on Israel
description: Iran launches 300+ drones and missiles at Israel in retaliation for the April 1 Damascus consulate strike; largely telegraphed for about two weeks, so surprise is low despite the scale. DRAFT coding.

title: Iran's October ballistic-missile strike on Israel
description: Iran fires about 180 ballistic missiles at Israel after the killing of Hezbollah's leader; the direct Iran-Israel exchange lifts the Middle East war premium and Hormuz risk. DRAFT coding.

title: Israel-Iran war onset (Operation Rising Lion)
description: Israel launches a wide air campaign against Iran's nuclear and military sites, opening a 12-day war; a direct attack on a major OPEC producer with acute Strait of Hormuz risk. DRAFT coding.

title: EU embargo on Iranian oil
description: Council Decision 2012/35/CFSP bans import purchase and transport of Iranian crude; phased with full effect 1 July 2012; heavily telegraphed for weeks beforehand. DRAFT coding.

title: US ends all Iran oil sanction waivers
description: Pompeo announces no renewal of significant-reduction exceptions for eight buyers of Iranian crude; markets had expected extensions; ~1 mb/d at stake. DRAFT coding.

title: US financial sanctions on Venezuela (EO 13808)
description: Executive Order 13808 bars dealings in new debt of PDVSA and the Venezuelan government; first financial-sector strike at the oil state; effective 25 Aug 2017. DRAFT coding.

title: Saudi Arabia suspends oil shipments through Bab el-Mandeb
description: After Houthi attacks on two Saudi tankers Riyadh halts all crude transit through the strait (~500-700 kb/d) until safety is restored. DRAFT coding.

title: Iran seizes British tanker Stena Impero in Hormuz
description: IRGC seizes UK-flagged tanker in the Strait of Hormuz at the peak of the 2019 tanker crisis; direct state interference with transit through the top oil chokepoint. DRAFT coding.

title: Tanker Bridgeton strikes Iranian mine in first Earnest Will convoy
description: Reflagged Kuwaiti supertanker hits IRGC mine near Farsi Island during first US-escorted convoy of the Tanker War. NOTE: daily Brent history begins mid-1987 so the estimation window may be too short - engine may drop this event; approving it is still safe. DRAFT coding.

title: Colonial Pipeline ransomware shutdown
description: Ransomware attack shuts the largest US refined-products pipeline (~45% of East Coast fuel) for five days; cyber rather than kinetic; products more than crude. DRAFT coding.

title: Houthi drone and missile attack on Ras Tanura
description: Drone strikes the worlds largest oil loading facility plus Aramco Dhahran compound; minimal physical damage but first direct hit at the heart of Saudi export infrastructure since Abqaiq. DRAFT coding.

title: OPEC Jakarta meeting raises production ceiling 10%
description: Conference of 26 Nov - 1 Dec 1997 lifts ceiling from 25 to 27.5 mb/d into the teeth of the Asian crisis; textbook pro-cyclical error preceding the 1998 price collapse. Dated to close of conference. DRAFT coding.

title: OPEC ratifies 1.7 mb/d production cut
description: Vienna meeting ratifies the Hague framework (agreed ~10 days earlier so partially telegraphed) totalling ~2.1 mb/d with non-OPEC; launched the 1999 price recovery. DRAFT coding.

title: OPEC+ announces 2 mb/d production cut
description: First in-person meeting since 2020 cuts quotas by 2 mb/d - largest since the pandemic - over explicit US objection; ~1 mb/d had been rumored so partially anticipated. DRAFT coding.

title: Thailand floats the baht - Asian crisis begins
description: Bank of Thailand abandons the dollar peg; baht falls 15-20% at once; the discrete dateable trigger of the Asian financial crisis and the 1997-98 oil demand collapse. DRAFT coding.

title: US Iran and Libya Sanctions Act signed
description: Clinton signs ILSA: sanctions on foreign firms investing >$20M/yr in Iranian (or >$40M Libyan) petroleum development; first US secondary-sanctions strike at partner-country energy investment. DRAFT coding.

title: US NDAA sanctions on Central Bank of Iran
description: NDAA Sec 1245 signed: blocks CBI and threatens sanctions on third-country banks settling Iranian oil trades - the financial chokehold on Iranian exports. Clusters with the EU embargo 23 days later; keep-first rule applies. DRAFT coding.

title: SWIFT disconnects Iranian banks
description: Unprecedented: SWIFT cuts 30 Iranian banks from international payments messaging under EU directive - the plumbing-level enforcement of the oil embargo. DRAFT coding.

title: US blocks all Venezuelan government property (EO 13884)
description: Full asset freeze on the Government of Venezuela incl. PDVSA and central bank - escalation from sectoral to near-total embargo. DRAFT coding.

title: G7 price cap on Russian petroleum products takes effect
description: Second-stage cap: $100/bbl premium products and $45/bbl discount products on seaborne Russian diesel/fuel oil, atop the December crude cap. DRAFT coding.

title: US sanctions Gazprom Neft Surgutneftegas and 183 shadow-fleet tankers
description: Largest tanker-sanctions action ever: OFAC hits two major producers plus 183 vessels incl. 69 Sovcomflot ships - direct strike at Russian export logistics. DRAFT coding.

title: IEA coordinated 60M bbl release after Katrina
description: All 26 IEA members offer 60M barrels over 30 days after Katrina wrecks Gulf production - second coordinated release in IEA history. DRAFT coding.

title: IEA coordinated 60M bbl release (Libya disruption)
description: Third-ever coordinated release: 60M barrels (30M US SPR) answering the Libyan outage - the buffer used as designed. DRAFT coding.

title: US-led six-nation coordinated SPR release (50M bbl)
description: First price-motivated coordinated release: US 50M with China India Japan Korea UK - buffers deployed against price not outage. DRAFT coding.

title: US announces record 180M bbl SPR release
description: Largest SPR release in history: 1M bbl/day for six months against the invasion price spike. Exactly 35 days after the invasion - clusters under keep-first rule; flagged. DRAFT coding.

title: ISIS captures Mosul and advances in northern Iraq
description: ISIS overran Mosul on 10 Jun 2014, threatening Iraqi output (a major OPEC producer) and lifting Brent to a nine-month high on supply-risk premium; southern fields (~90% of output) stayed safe. Mechanism: risk premium on a major producer's supply.

title: JCPOA nuclear deal reached; path to lifting Iran oil sanctions
description: Iran and P5+1 agreed the JCPOA on 14 Jul 2015, opening the way to lift oil-related sanctions and return Iranian barrels to market (bearish supply). Telegraphed by the April 2015 framework. Mechanism: future supply increase from a sanctioned producer.

title: Implementation Day: Iran oil sanctions lifted
description: On 16 Jan 2016 the IAEA verified Iran's steps and nuclear-related oil sanctions were lifted, letting Iran ramp exports back toward pre-sanction levels (bearish). Expected after the JCPOA. Mechanism: actual supply return from a sanctioned producer.

title: Iraqi forces seize oil-rich Kirkuk from Kurds
description: After the 25 Sep 2017 Kurdish independence referendum, Iraqi forces retook Kirkuk on 16 Oct 2017, disrupting ~0.5 mb/d of Kurdish exports via the Kirkuk-Ceyhan line. Mechanism: military seizure disrupting an export route.

title: Four tankers sabotaged off Fujairah near Hormuz
description: Limpet-mine sabotage damaged four tankers off Fujairah on 12 May 2019 just outside the Strait of Hormuz; no output lost but it raised the Gulf-shipping risk premium. Mechanism: attack on export vessels near a critical chokepoint.

title: OPEC emergency 1.5 mb/d cut in the financial crisis
description: OPEC brought forward an emergency Vienna meeting and cut 1.5 mb/d on 24 Oct 2008 to arrest a price collapse (Brent had fallen ~56% from the July peak). Widely expected given the crash. Mechanism: supply cut by the cartel.

title: Pro-Haftar forces blockade Libya's oil export terminals
description: On 18 Jan 2020 pro-Haftar forces blockaded Libya's eastern export terminals and southern fields, cutting output from ~1.2 mb/d to ~0.32 mb/d. Mechanism: blockade of export terminals removing supply.

title: OPEC agrees first 1998 production cut in Vienna
description: OPEC's 104th extraordinary meeting cut output by 1.245 million bpd effective April 1 to defend collapsing prices, tightening crude supply as Asian-crisis demand fell

title: OPEC deepens 1998 cuts at Amsterdam-era conference
description: At its 105th conference OPEC agreed a further 1.355 million bpd cut effective July 1, lifting cumulative 1998 reductions to 2.6 million bpd to arrest the price slide

title: OPEC raises quotas 1.452 million bpd
description: OPEC agreed to increase production by 1.452 million bpd (excluding Iran and Iraq) to cool prices that had recovered sharply, loosening supply into the market

title: OPEC lifts quotas 708000 bpd in Vienna
description: OPEC raised production quotas by 708,000 bpd to a 25.4 million bpd ceiling effective July 1, adding barrels as prices stayed firm

title: OPEC boosts quotas 800000 bpd
description: OPEC increased quotas by 800,000 bpd to 26.2 million bpd effective October 1 to tame high prices ahead of winter, easing supply tightness

title: OPEC cuts quotas 1.5 million bpd
description: OPEC agreed to reduce members' production quotas by 1.5 million bpd as demand weakened, the first of three 2001 cuts to defend prices

title: OPEC cuts output 1 million bpd effective April
description: OPEC decided to cut output by about 1 million bpd (4%) effective April 1 as the global slowdown sapped oil demand, tightening supply to arrest falling prices

title: OPEC cuts 1 million bpd effective September
description: OPEC ministers agreed to cut crude production by about 1 million bpd effective September 1 amid falling prices, the third 2001 reduction ahead of the demand slump later deepened by 9/11

title: OPEC agrees 1.5 million bpd cut in Cairo
description: OPEC ministers meeting in Cairo agreed to cut output quotas by 1.5 million bpd (about 6.5%) for six months from January 1 2002, conditional on non-OPEC cuts

title: OPEC raises quota 6.5% amid Venezuela strike
description: OPEC lifted its ceiling to 24.5 million bpd (a 6.5% increase) effective February 1 to replace barrels lost to the Venezuelan oil strike and pre-Iraq-war supply fears

title: OPEC holds emergency Iraq-war meeting
description: In Vienna emergency talks OPEC set a 25.4 million bpd quota while cutting actual production by 2 million bpd from June 1 to absorb returning Iraqi supply after the US invasion

title: OPEC surprises with 900000 bpd cut
description: OPEC unexpectedly cut its ceiling by 900,000 bpd to 24.5 million bpd effective November 1, a surprise tightening given firm demand

title: OPEC raises quotas 2 million bpd in Beirut
description: OPEC ministers in Beirut agreed to raise quotas by a combined 2 million bpd from July 1 plus a further 500,000 bpd from August 1 to calm prices near record highs

title: OPEC trims output 1 million bpd
description: At its quarterly meeting OPEC agreed to lower production by 1 million bpd effective January 1 2005 to defend against seasonal price softening

title: OPEC cuts 500000 bpd at Abuja
description: Meeting in Abuja OPEC agreed a 500,000 bpd cut effective February 2007, a second-stage reduction after October to draw down high consumer stocks

title: OPEC announces record 2.2 million bpd cut at Oran
description: At its 151st extraordinary meeting in Oran OPEC agreed its largest-ever single cut of 2.2 million bpd effective January 2009 to halt the demand-driven price collapse

title: OPEC fails to agree output increase in Vienna
description: OPEC broke up without a deal after Saudi Arabia's push to add up to 1.5 million bpd was blocked by Iran and Venezuela, leaving supply constrained

title: OPEC reaches Algiers accord to cut output
description: At the 170th meeting in Algiers OPEC agreed in principle to cut output to 32.5-33.0 million bpd, its first cut framework since 2008, later finalized in November

title: OPEC extends cuts nine months in Vienna
description: OPEC and non-OPEC allies agreed to extend the 1.8 million bpd cuts by nine months to March 2018 to drain the global glut; the widely expected outcome kept supply restrained

title: OPEC+ agrees to raise output about 1 million bpd
description: After contentious Vienna talks OPEC agreed to nominally boost output by about 1 million bpd by returning to full quota compliance, loosening supply amid US pressure

title: OPEC+ agrees 1.2 million bpd cut in Vienna
description: OPEC and non-OPEC allies agreed a combined 1.2 million bpd cut for six months from January 2019, a larger-than-expected tightening to counter a price slide

title: OPEC+ extends record cuts through July
description: OPEC+ agreed to extend the record 9.6-9.7 million bpd cuts by one month to end-July, prolonging the pandemic-era supply withdrawal

title: OPEC+ talks collapse over UAE baseline dispute
description: OPEC+ cancelled its meeting with no new date after the UAE blocked a deal to add 400,000 bpd/month, leaving planned supply increases stalled

title: Saudi Arabia announces extra 1 million bpd voluntary cut
description: At the June OPEC+ meeting Saudi Arabia announced an additional voluntary 1 million bpd cut for July taking its output to about 9 million bpd to unilaterally tighten supply

title: OPEC+ agrees 2.2 million bpd voluntary cuts
description: Several OPEC+ members announced combined voluntary cuts totaling 2.2 million bpd for Q1 2024 including Saudi Arabia's 1 million bpd, a fragmented tightening markets met with skepticism

title: UN Resolution 661 oil embargo on Iraq
description: UN Security Council imposed comprehensive sanctions including a total oil embargo on Iraq after its invasion of Kuwait, removing roughly 4 mb/d of Iraqi and Kuwaiti crude from world supply

title: US total trade embargo on Iran (EO 12959)
description: Clinton's Executive Order 12959 imposed a total US trade and investment ban on Iran, barring US firms from Iranian oil development

title: UN Resolution 986 oil-for-food adopted
description: UN Security Council adopted Resolution 986 permitting limited Iraqi oil exports to fund humanitarian imports, easing the total embargo

title: Iraq oil-for-food exports begin
description: First Iraqi oil exports under the oil-for-food program began, returning capped volumes of Iraqi crude to the world market for the first time since the 1990 embargo

title: UN lifts Iraq sanctions (Resolution 1483)
description: UN Security Council adopted Resolution 1483 lifting economic sanctions on Iraq, freeing post-war Iraqi oil sales into open markets

title: US lifts most Libya sanctions
description: The Bush administration terminated ILSA application and eased sanctions on Libya after its WMD renunciation, reopening Libyan oil fields to US majors

title: Iran CISADA sanctions signed
description: President Obama signed CISADA, penalizing firms supplying Iran's refined petroleum and petroleum-sector investment, tightening pressure on Iranian oil

title: US sectoral sanctions on Russian energy (EO 13662)
description: US Treasury imposed first sectoral sanctions restricting new financing for Rosneft and Novatek under EO 13662, constraining Russian oil-sector capital

title: US and EU ban Russian Arctic deepwater shale oil tech
description: US and EU barred exports of oil-extraction technology and services for Russian Arctic, deepwater and shale projects, targeting five majors including Rosneft and Lukoil

title: First Iran sanctions wind-down after JCPOA exit
description: First tranche of reimposed US Iran sanctions took effect after the JCPOA withdrawal, hitting metals and autos ahead of the November oil snapback

title: US reimposes Iran oil sanctions with waivers
description: US reimposed energy, shipping and banking sanctions on Iran but granted 180-day oil-import waivers to eight buyers, tempering the supply shock

title: US sanctions Iran's largest petrochemical group
description: OFAC designated Persian Gulf Petrochemical Industries Company and 39 subsidiaries, targeting about 40% of Iran's petrochemical capacity and export revenue

title: US sanctions Rosneft Trading over Venezuela oil
description: OFAC designated Rosneft Trading SA under EO 13850 for handling roughly half of Venezuela's crude exports, squeezing the main channel for Venezuelan oil sales

title: US sanctions Sovcomflot tankers over price-cap breach
description: OFAC sanctioned three Sovcomflot crude tankers for carrying Russian oil above the G7 price cap, tightening enforcement of the cap

title: US eases Venezuela oil sanctions (General License 44)
description: OFAC issued GL 44 authorizing Venezuelan oil and gas sector transactions after the Barbados agreement, temporarily reopening Venezuelan crude to markets

title: US reimposes Venezuela oil sanctions (GL 44 revoked)
description: OFAC let GL 44 lapse and issued wind-down license GL 44A after Maduro blocked a competitive election, reimposing oil-sector sanctions on Venezuela

title: US Navy Operation Praying Mantis strikes Iranian oil platforms
description: US forces destroyed two Iranian oil platforms and sank Iranian vessels during the Tanker War, raising fears of Gulf oil-supply and shipping disruption

title: Insurgents bomb Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline halting northern Iraq exports
description: An explosion at Al-Fateha west of Kirkuk halted crude flow through Iraq's northern export pipeline to Ceyhan, removing Iraqi export supply

title: Saboteurs halt southern Iraq oil exports in late-August 2004
description: Attacks on southern pipelines ceased oil flows carrying about 90% of Iraq's exports, cutting roughly 1.9 mb/d of supply for about a week

title: MEND attacks Shell Forcados terminal cutting Nigeria exports
description: MEND damaged Shell's Forcados export terminal and pipelines, forcing suspension of about 400,000 b/d of crude exports and cutting Nigerian exports by a fifth

title: Al-Qaeda suicide car-bomb attack on Saudi Abqaiq foiled
description: Suicide bombers attempted to breach the world's largest crude processing facility handling about two-thirds of Saudi output; guards repelled them but exposed a supply-chokepoint vulnerability

title: MEND attacks Shell Bonga offshore FPSO
description: MEND militants reached Shell's Bonga FPSO about 120km offshore and forced a shutdown of 225,000 b/d, prompting a force majeure on June-July exports

title: South Sudan seizes Sudan's Heglig oil field
description: South Sudan's army captured Heglig, about half of Sudan's remaining output, escalating cross-border fighting and cutting regional crude production

title: Niger Delta Avengers bomb Trans Forcados subsea pipeline
description: The first attack on a Nigerian subsea pipeline shut the Trans Forcados line feeding the 400,000 b/d Forcados terminal, forcing a Shell force majeure

title: Niger Delta Avengers bomb Chevron Escravos facilities
description: Avengers destroyed the Escravos tank farm feed and other lines, helping push Nigerian production down about 800,000 b/d to a 20-year low

title: Armed offensive seizes Libya's Es Sider and Ras Lanuf oil ports
description: Fighters under Ibrahim Jedran stormed the Es Sider and Ras Lanuf export terminals, closing them and cutting about 240,000 b/d

title: Houthi drones strike Saudi East-West crude pipeline
description: Armed drones hit two pump stations on the East-West pipeline that carries Saudi crude to the Red Sea, briefly halting pumping and signaling deep-strike reach

title: Houthi drones strike Saudi Shaybah oil and gas field
description: Houthis struck the 1 mb/d Shaybah field and its gas facility near the UAE border, causing a limited fire and demonstrating extended strike range

title: Houthi cruise missile hits Aramco North Jeddah fuel depot
description: A Quds-2 cruise missile struck a 500,000-barrel fuel storage tank at Aramco's North Jeddah plant, causing major roof damage but no supply loss

title: Houthi drone-missile attack hits ADNOC Musaffah fuel facility
description: Drones and missiles struck ADNOC fuel trucks at Musaffah in Abu Dhabi, killing three and marking the first confirmed Houthi strike on UAE oil infrastructure

title: Houthi strike sets Aramco Jeddah oil depot ablaze during F1 weekend
description: Houthi drones and missiles set two storage tanks at Aramco's North Jeddah plant on fire during the Formula 1 Grand Prix, a high-visibility strike on Saudi fuel logistics

title: Ukraine drone strike ignites Novatek Ust-Luga Baltic export terminal
description: A drone strike sparked a major fire at Novatek's Ust-Luga complex, halting gas-condensate processing and opening Ukraine's deep-strike campaign on Russian energy exports

title: Ukraine escalates drone strikes on Russian refineries
description: Drones hit Rosneft's Ryazan and the Novoshakhtinsk refineries, part of a campaign that knocked out roughly 17% of Russian refining capacity by April 2024

title: Tanker Tropic Brilliance runs aground and blocks the Suez Canal
description: The 89000-tonne oil tanker lodged crosswise near Ismailiya, closing the Suez Canal for three days and halting up to 60 ships including crude cargoes

title: Iran threatens to close the Strait of Hormuz
description: Iran's vice president threatened to shut Hormuz in response to looming EU/US oil sanctions, putting the roughly 17 mb/d transit chokepoint at risk

title: Jathran's guards blockade Libya's eastern export terminals
description: Petroleum Facilities Guard forces shut Es Sider, Ras Lanuf and Zueitina export terminals over a revenue dispute, choking off roughly 600,000 b/d of Libyan export capacity

title: ISIS attacks sever the Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline
description: Repeated ISIS bombing knocked out the Iraqi leg of the Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline, cutting northern Iraqi crude flows to the Mediterranean by roughly 0.4 mb/d

title: Armed clashes force closure of Libya's Es Sider and Ras Lanuf oil ports
description: Fighting between rival Libyan factions at the eastern export terminals shut Es Sider and Ras Lanuf, removing several hundred thousand b/d of export capacity

title: Houthis attack a Saudi crude tanker near the Bab-el-Mandeb approaches
description: Houthi forces attacked a Saudi oil tanker off Hodeidah near Bab-el-Mandeb, threatening the Red Sea transit route for Gulf-to-Europe crude

title: Royal Marines seize Iranian tanker Grace 1 off Gibraltar
description: British forces seized the Iranian-laden supertanker Grace 1 off Gibraltar for suspected sanctions-busting, escalating tanker-seizure tit-for-tat that threatened Hormuz transit

title: Contaminated crude halts the Druzhba pipeline to Europe
description: Organic-chloride contamination forced suspension of the roughly 1 mb/d Druzhba pipeline, cutting Russian crude flows to refiners in Germany, Poland, Slovakia and Hungary

title: Drone attack strikes tanker Mercer Street off Oman
description: An Iranian-attributed one-way-drone strike hit the tanker Mercer Street off Oman, killing two and raising war-risk premiums on the Gulf-of-Oman/Hormuz route

title: Iran seizes South Korean tanker Hankuk Chemi in the Strait of Hormuz
description: Iran's IRGC seized the tanker Hankuk Chemi transiting Hormuz, reasserting the threat of Iranian interdiction on the world's key oil transit chokepoint

title: Storm damage halts Kazakh crude exports at the CPC Novorossiysk terminal
description: Storm damage to single-point moorings stopped loadings at the CPC Black Sea terminal that handles about 80% of Kazakh crude exports, threatening roughly 1 mb/d for weeks

title: Turkey halts Iraqi Kurdistan crude exports at Ceyhan
description: An ICC arbitration ruling led Turkey to stop the Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline, removing about 450,000 b/d of KRG crude from the Mediterranean market

title: Ukrainian drone strike on CPC Kropotkinskaya pumping station
description: A drone attack severely damaged a key CPC pumping station, cutting throughput of Kazakh crude to Novorossiysk by roughly 30-40% with repairs expected to take months

title: South Korea requests IMF bailout
description: South Korea formally sought an IMF rescue as the Asian financial crisis deepened, signaling regional recession that curtailed Asian petroleum imports and cut oil demand growth

title: Russian sovereign default and LTCM crisis
description: Russia defaulted on domestic debt and let the ruble collapse, triggering a global flight from risk and the LTCM blowup that deepened fears of weaker world growth and oil demand

title: Clinton orders 30M-barrel SPR swap release
description: President Clinton ordered the release of 30 million barrels from the US SPR on a swap basis to boost heating oil supply and pressure prices ahead of winter

title: US 2001 recession onset (dot-com bust)
description: The NBER-dated US recession beginning March 2001 slashed petroleum product demand growth to near zero, weakening the global oil demand outlook

title: Bush signs halt to SPR deposits
description: With Congress voting to suspend SPR fills, Bush signed a six-month halt to deliveries, freeing roughly 13M barrels back to the market to ease record-high oil prices

title: China yuan devaluation raises demand fears
description: The PBOC's surprise devaluation of the yuan raised the cost of dollar-priced crude imports and stoked fears of falling Chinese oil demand

title: IMF cuts global growth on trade war
description: The IMF's October WEO downgraded 2018-19 global growth citing US trade tensions, crystallizing the demand-side growth scare that pressured oil through Q4 2018

title: Trump orders SPR filled to the top
description: Trump directed DOE to buy crude to fill the SPR amid the COVID demand collapse, a demand-side intervention before funding was blocked

title: India tops up strategic reserve at low prices
description: India moved to fill its three strategic petroleum reserves with cheap crude (16.7M barrels), adding demand-side support to the market

title: China announces first-ever state oil reserve release
description: China's reserve bureau announced its first strategic crude auction (7.38M barrels) to ease refiner input costs, a landmark demand-side policy intervention

title: IEA coordinated 60M-barrel emergency release
description: All 31 IEA member countries agreed to release 60 million barrels from strategic reserves after Russia's invasion of Ukraine to signal no supply shortfall

title: Shanghai COVID lockdown hits China oil demand
description: Shanghai's phased lockdown of about 25M people revived fears of lost demand in the world's largest oil importer, cutting jet, gasoline and diesel consumption

title: IEA 120M-barrel second coordinated release
description: The IEA announced a second coordinated release of 120 million barrels within a month to counter war-driven supply disruption and high prices

title: DOE begins SPR refill with 3M-barrel buyback
description: DOE announced its first repurchase of 3M barrels to begin replenishing the SPR after the record 180M-barrel drawdown, a shift to demand-side buying

title: SVB collapse sparks banking-stress demand fears
description: Silicon Valley Bank's failure ignited a banking panic and risk-asset exodus, raising recession and oil-demand fears

title: MEND attacks Shell Niger Delta oil facilities
description: Militant kidnapping and pipeline sabotage forced Shell to shut in about 226,000 bpd and suspend Forcados exports, removing Nigerian light crude from the seaborne market

title: Baku-Tbilisi-Ceyhan pipeline explosion in Turkey
description: An explosion and fire at Refahiye shut the 1 mb/d BTC pipeline carrying Caspian crude to the Mediterranean for about three weeks, cutting non-OPEC export flow

title: Venezuela nationwide blackout halts oil exports
description: A prolonged power failure shut the Jose terminal and Orinoco upgraders, halting tanker loadings and briefly cutting national crude output by half

title: Iraq suspends oil exports for 30 days
description: Iraq halted roughly 1.8 mb/d of official crude exports for 30 days to protest Israel's West Bank incursion, withdrawing about 2% of global supply

title: Gulf states impose diplomatic and transport blockade on Qatar
description: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt and Bahrain cut ties and closed land/air/sea links to Qatar, raising Gulf shipping and oil/LNG transit-risk premiums

title: OPEC+ agrees deeper 500kbd production cut
description: OPEC+ deepened output cuts by an extra ~500 kb/d to about 1.7 mb/d total for Q1 2020, tightening supply ahead of the Aramco IPO

title: OPEC+ accelerates output hike to 648kbd
description: OPEC+ pulled forward September's increase, lifting July and August output by about 648 kb/d each to ease a tight post-invasion market

title: OPEC+ announces gradual unwind of voluntary cuts
description: OPEC+ laid out a plan to phase 2.2 mb/d of voluntary cuts back into the market from October 2024, a bearish forward-supply signal

title: OPEC+ delays output-hike revival to April 2025
description: OPEC+ pushed the start of its 2.2 mb/d supply unwind from January to April 2025 and slowed the pace, keeping barrels off the market longer

title: Retreating Iraqi forces torch Kuwaiti oil wells
description: Iraqi forces set fire to 600-730 Kuwaiti oil wells during their retreat, removing more than 1.5 mb/d of Kuwaiti output for months

title: Nigeria Warri unrest forces Niger Delta oil shut-in
description: Ijaw militia attacks forced Chevron and Shell to evacuate and shut in about 800 kb/d of Nigerian light-sweet crude

title: Russian state auctions Yukos unit Yuganskneftegaz
description: A forced state auction of Yukos's core ~1 mb/d production unit raised expropriation and supply-continuity risk on Russian crude exports

title: Turkish ground incursion into northern Iraq
description: Turkey's Operation Sun near the Kirkuk-Ceyhan export corridor raised the risk of disruption to northern Iraqi crude exports

title: Egyptian revolution erupts raising Suez transit risk
description: Mass unrest in Egypt threatened closure of the Suez Canal and SUMED pipeline, chokepoints for about 1.8 mb/d of crude and products

title: Egyptian military ousts Morsi reviving Suez fears
description: The coup and unrest at the Suez Canal and SUMED chokepoint renewed fears of disruption to crude and product transit

title: Houthis resume Red Sea attacks sinking Magic Seas
description: Renewed Houthi attacks near Bab-el-Mandeb revived the shipping-risk premium and Cape rerouting for oil flows through the chokepoint

title: OPEC holds output ceiling at Kuwait meeting
description: At its 139th Conference in Kuwait City OPEC left its 28 mb/d ceiling unchanged, declining to tighten supply and keeping crude flows steady into a firm market.

title: OPEC agrees 500000 bpd output increase effective November
description: At its 145th Conference in Vienna OPEC agreed to raise production by about 500,000 b/d from 1 November, adding barrels to a tight market to cap rising prices.

title: OPEC keeps production quotas unchanged in Vienna
description: At its 153rd Conference OPEC held quotas near 24.9 mb/d, declining to add supply and leaving the market to rebalance as prices recovered.

title: OPEC sets 30 million bpd production ceiling
description: At its 160th Conference OPEC set a collective ceiling of 30 mb/d, formalising higher output to absorb returning post-war Libyan barrels into supply.

title: OPEC rolls over 30 million bpd ceiling in Vienna
description: At its 161st Conference OPEC kept the 30 mb/d ceiling unchanged despite overproduction, leaving abundant supply on the market amid eurozone demand fears.

title: OPEC maintains 30 million bpd output ceiling
description: At its 163rd Conference in Vienna OPEC held the 30 mb/d ceiling, keeping supply steady on caution over weak global demand.

title: OPEC keeps 30 million bpd ceiling at 164th meeting
description: At its 164th Conference OPEC maintained the 30 mb/d ceiling, leaving output allocations unchanged and supply steady into 2014.

title: OPEC drops output ceiling and fails to agree a limit
description: At its 168th Conference OPEC abandoned any formal production ceiling as members refused curbs, signalling continued oversupply in the market-share war.

title: OPEC+ talks collapse over UAE quota dispute
description: OPEC+ ministerial talks broke down after the UAE blocked a proposed 400,000 b/d monthly increase, leaving supply policy in limbo.

title: OPEC+ sticks to 400000 bpd hike despite Ukraine war
description: OPEC+ rubber-stamped a 400,000 b/d April increase in a brief meeting, declining to add extra supply as war-driven prices surged.

title: Eight OPEC+ producers triple planned May output hike
description: Eight OPEC+ producers unexpectedly accelerated their unwind, adding 411,000 b/d in May versus an expected ~140,000 b/d, pushing more supply onto the market.

title: US signs EO 13590 targeting Iran energy sector
description: Executive Order 13590 authorised sanctions on suppliers to Iran's petroleum and petrochemical sectors, tightening pressure on Iranian oil development and exports.

title: JPOA interim deal pauses Iran oil sanctions
description: The P5+1 Joint Plan of Action paused further cuts to Iranian crude exports for six months, easing supply pressure by letting existing buyers maintain purchases.

title: US designates Iran IRGC as a Foreign Terrorist Organization
description: The State Department designated the IRGC as an FTO, raising legal risk for entities trading Iranian oil linked to IRGC networks and tightening export channels.

title: EU adopts 6th package with Russian seaborne oil embargo
description: The EU banned seaborne imports of Russian crude and products (~90% of imports), forcing a large redirection of Russian oil flows and tightening Atlantic supply.

title: EU 8th package lays basis for Russian oil price cap
description: The EU's eighth package established the legal framework for the G7 price cap, banning maritime services for Russian oil sold above the cap and reshaping flows.

title: US sanctions Russian state tanker group Sovcomflot
description: OFAC designated Sovcomflot and identified 14 crude tankers under EO 14024, disrupting Russia's shipping capacity and raising the cost of moving its oil.

title: US widens secondary sanctions on Iran petroleum sector
description: OFAC issued a determination targeting Iran's petroleum and petrochemical sectors after Iran's missile attack on Israel, raising secondary-sanction risk on Iranian oil buyers.

title: Ukrainian drone strike on Rosneft Tuapse refinery
description: Overnight drone attack damaged distillation columns at Rosneft's 240kbd Black Sea Tuapse refinery, cutting Russian refined-product output and export supply.

title: Ukrainian drone strike on Lukoil Volgograd refinery
description: SBU drones hit primary processing units at Lukoil's Volgograd refinery, the largest products producer in Russia's South district, disrupting crude runs and fuel supply.

title: Ukrainian drone strike on Slavyansk-on-Kuban refinery
description: Eight drones hit the distillation units at the export-oriented Slavyansk refinery in Krasnodar, halting operations and cutting refined-product supply.

title: Ukrainian drone strike on Novorossiysk oil depots
description: Overnight drones damaged two oil depots and two terminals at Novorossiysk, disrupting Black Sea crude storage and export flows.

title: Ukrainian drone strike sets Rosneft Tuapse refinery on fire
description: Drone attack set fire to the 240kbd Rosneft Tuapse refinery, cutting Russian refined-product export supply.

title: Ukrainian strike sparks blaze at Novoshakhtinsk refinery
description: More than three dozen drones and three missiles sparked a blaze at the Novoshakhtinsk refinery, the largest products supplier in southern Russia, disrupting fuel output.

title: Ukrainian mass drone strike on Rosneft Ryazan refinery
description: Ukraine's largest drone attack of the year set ablaze the Rosneft Ryazan refinery, one of Russia's five largest, forcing a suspension of crude processing.

title: Ukrainian drone strike on Lukoil Volgograd refinery
description: Overnight drones sparked a fire at Lukoil's Volgograd refinery, one of Russia's largest, disrupting crude runs and southern fuel supply.

title: Ukrainian drone strike on Rosneft Novokuibyshevsk refinery
description: Drones struck Rosneft's Novokuibyshevsk refinery in Samara, the most powerful plant of the Samara group, disrupting crude processing and fuel output.

title: Ukrainian drone strike halts Rosneft Saratov refinery
description: Drone strike forced the Rosneft Saratov refinery to halt crude intake, the third Rosneft plant disrupted in a week amid a domestic fuel crunch.

title: Ukrainian strike halts Druzhba pipeline oil flow to Hungary and Slovakia
description: Drone strikes on the Unecha Druzhba pumping hub halted Russian crude flows to Hungary and Slovakia for several days, disrupting a major export route.

title: Ukrainian drone strike on Rosneft Ryazan refinery
description: Repeat drone strike on the Rosneft Ryazan refinery deepened a wave of outages estimated to knock out ~1.1 mbd of refining capacity.

title: Ukrainian drone strike halts oil loadings at Novorossiysk Sheskharis terminal
description: Drones hit the Sheskharis complex; Transneft halted crude flows into Novorossiysk and the port stopped loading oil, lifting oil prices on supply fears.

title: Houthis seize Galaxy Leader car carrier in Red Sea
description: Houthi raid seizes a commercial vessel in the southern Red Sea, opening a campaign that raises Bab-el-Mandeb transit risk and insurance costs for oil-carrying traffic.

title: Houthi drone strike triggers Red Sea shipping diversions
description: A Houthi attack near Bab-el-Mandeb triggers major carriers to pause and reroute around the Cape, cutting crude and product flows and lengthening oil supply chains.

title: US and UK launch first airstrikes on Houthi targets in Yemen
description: About 70 US/UK strikes on Houthi missile and drone sites mark direct Western involvement, escalating Red Sea conflict risk and the oil geopolitical risk premium.

title: Houthi missile sets tanker Marlin Luanda ablaze in Gulf of Aden
description: A Houthi ballistic missile strikes the naphtha-laden tanker Marlin Luanda, igniting a cargo tank and confirming petroleum tankers as direct targets on the Red Sea route.

title: Houthi missile cripples Rubymar, the first ship sunk in the Red Sea crisis
description: A Houthi missile strikes the bulk carrier Rubymar, which is abandoned and later sinks, underscoring the physical closure risk to the Bab-el-Mandeb oil transit lane.

title: Israel airstrike destroys Iran consulate in Damascus
description: Israeli strike killing IRGC commanders at Iran's Damascus consulate opens a direct Israel-Iran escalation cycle, raising the oil risk premium on Gulf supply fears.

title: Houthi attack sinks bulk carrier MV Tutor in the Red Sea
description: A Houthi drone-boat and missile attack fatally damages the carrier MV Tutor, the second Red Sea sinking, deepening avoidance of the Bab-el-Mandeb oil lane.

title: Houthi drone boat hits tanker Chios Lion
description: A Houthi unmanned surface vessel damages the tanker Chios Lion, producing a large oil slick and reinforcing the tanker-targeting threat on the Red Sea route.

title: Hamas leader Ismail Haniyeh assassinated in Tehran
description: Haniyeh's killing on Iranian soil prompts vows of direct retaliation against Israel, raising the odds of a regional war that could disrupt Gulf oil supply.

title: Houthis set crude tanker Sounion ablaze in the Red Sea
description: Houthi attacks disable and set fire to the Sounion carrying 150,000 tonnes of crude, threatening a massive spill and showing the acute risk to loaded crude tankers.

title: Israeli airstrike kills Hezbollah leader Hassan Nasrallah
description: The killing of Nasrallah in a large Beirut strike escalates the Israel-Hezbollah-Iran axis conflict, raising the probability of a wider war threatening Gulf oil.

title: Israel strikes Iranian military sites in Operation Days of Repentance
description: Israel's largest strikes on Iran since the Iran-Iraq war hit military sites but deliberately avoid oil and nuclear facilities, testing but not disrupting Iranian crude.

title: US launches Operation Rough Rider air campaign against Yemen Houthis
description: Trump orders large-scale near-daily US strikes on Houthi targets to reopen the Red Sea, escalating US-Houthi conflict and sustaining risk to the Bab-el-Mandeb corridor.

title: US strikes Iranian nuclear sites Fordow Natanz and Isfahan
description: In Operation Midnight Hammer the US bombs three Iranian nuclear sites, directly entering the Israel-Iran war and spiking the oil risk premium on Hormuz disruption fears.

title: Nigeria offers MEND militants amnesty
description: A Nigerian government amnesty disarmed thousands of Niger Delta militants, ending sabotage that had cut ~25% of Nigerian crude output and easing a supply-risk premium.

title: Niger Delta Avengers hit Bonny Soku gas line
description: The militants' first claimed 2016 attack began a sabotage campaign that cut Nigerian output by roughly a third toward 1.4 mbd, tightening light-sweet crude supply.

title: US lifts 40-year crude oil export ban
description: The Consolidated Appropriations Act repealed the crude export ban, letting US barrels reach world markets and compressing the Brent-WTI spread.

title: WTI front-month settles negative at minus 37 dollars
description: COVID demand collapse plus full Cushing storage forced May WTI holders to pay to offload barrels, driving the front month below zero for the first time.

title: Protesters shut Iraq Nasiriya oil field
description: Anti-government protesters cut power and took the 90,000 bpd Nasiriya field offline, the first full field shut-in of Iraq's 2019 unrest, adding southern supply risk.

title: Fukushima quake shifts Japan to oil-fired power
description: The March 11 quake idled Japanese nuclear plants, roughly doubling direct-burn crude and fuel-oil use for power generation and lifting oil-import demand.

title: First US-China tariffs take effect
description: US 25% tariffs on $34bn of Chinese goods and China's retaliation on US crude took effect July 6, denting demand expectations and pressuring US crude prices.

title: Clashes shut Libya Es Sider and Ras Lanuf ports
description: Fighting near Libya's two largest export terminals from mid-December shut ~600,000 bpd of capacity, deepening Libyan supply outages.

title: US and China agree 90-day trade truce at G20
description: The Trump-Xi Buenos Aires truce paused tariff escalation, easing demand-destruction fears and supporting an oil rebound.

title: China unveils PBOC stimulus package
description: PBOC rate and reserve cuts lifted expectations for demand from the top crude importer, sending oil up over 2% to a three-week high.

title: Armed group shuts Libya El Sharara field
description: Libya's NOC declared force majeure after tribesmen seized the 315,000 bpd El Sharara field, removing Libya's largest field from supply for months.

title: Haftar conditionally lifts Libya oil blockade
description: Haftar's announcement ended an eight-month blockade, allowing Libyan output to recover from ~90,000 bpd toward pre-blockade levels and adding supply.
